basis: White-matter degeneration; optic atrophy 2/2. Associated ovarian insufficiency is supported by primary and secondary amenorrhea, each reported in 1/2.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: ovarian insufficiency is a recognized component of vanishing-white-matter disease; primary and secondary amenorrhea each occur in 1/2 annotated patients.

basis: Lysosomal lipid storage with defining hepatic steatosis/fibrosis; intestinal storage causes steatorrhea (80-99% HPO). Cognitive injury is atypical; atherosclerosis is separately coded.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic lipid accumulation with progressive liver injury is a defining manifestation across the principal LAL-deficiency subtypes.

basis: Hypomyelinating neurodegeneration; cataract, hypothyroidism and flexion contracture each reported in 1/1. Low B-cell count alone does not establish functional immunodeficiency.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent flexion contracture represents structural joint impairment and is documented in 1/1 patient; evidence remains limited to one case.

basis: Brainstem/cerebellar malformations, thoracic skeletal dysplasia and restrictive respiratory failure define the syndrome. Renal dysfunction and retinal dystrophy occur in 5-29%.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: respiratory failure from the narrow thorax is explicitly part of the disease definition, rather than an incidental respiratory symptom.

basis: Hereditary motor-sensory neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy in 21/21 and pes cavus in 19/21. A biochemical glycolytic disorder is not established for this HK1 neuropathy.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: the HK1-associated neuropathy lacks an established biochemical metabolic phenotype; glycolysis ancestry alone does not establish metabolic disease.

basis: Brain malformations and respiratory insufficiency define the syndrome. Fetal akinesia deformation sequence, reported in 3/3, includes congenital joint contractures.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: fetal akinesia sequence is a defining component and denotes congenital contractures and deformation, beyond reduced movement alone; reported in 3/3.

basis: Mitochondrial myopathy and diabetes define disease; pyramidal dysfunction is supported by Babinski sign (1/1) and lower-limb hyperreflexia (30-79%). Neuropathy is only 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: involved: Babinski sign plus frequent lower-limb hyperreflexia (30-79%) supports central motor-pathway dysfunction; inclusion does not depend on occasional neuropathy.

basis: Developmental and skeletal abnormalities characterize the syndrome; urinary abnormalities are annotated 80-99%. Myopia 4/8 and strabismus 6/14 support ocular involvement.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal abnormalities are explicitly characteristic in the definition; frequent structural hand/chest abnormalities and joint stiffness reinforce this assignment.

basis: Leptin-signalling deficiency causes obesity, hypogonadism and functional T-cell defects (80-99% HPO). Autonomic dysfunction with orthostatic hypotension is reported in 30-79%.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: impaired T-cell activation and CD4 deficits (80-99%), with recurrent infections (30-79%), establish an immunodeficiency component; the mechanism axis belongs in primary.

basis: Malignant glomus tumor derives from specialized vascular smooth-muscle cells of glomus bodies. Variable deep or visceral sites do not establish another organ axis.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: glomus cells are specialized vascular smooth-muscle cells; the tumor's vascular lineage supports this axis despite variable anatomical sites.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: subfascial location alone does not establish origin in skeletal muscle, bone, joints or locomotor connective tissue; glomus cells have vascular smooth-muscle lineage.
